newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court rejects IRA bombers' appeals.
newsitem.headline: German court rejects IRA bombers' appeals.

text.p: Germany's highest criminal court said on Thursday it had rejected an appeal by three Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas against their conviction for bombing a British army barracks in Germany.

The Federal Court of Justice in Karlsruhe upheld the ruling of a court in Celle, which sentenced Pauline and Donagh O'Kane and Patrick Murray to jail terms between nine and 10-1/4 years for blowing up the barracks in Osnabrueck in 1989.
It gave no reason for its decision.
Last May the court rejected an appeal by another IRA guerrilla, Donna Maguire, against her nine-year sentence in connection with the same bombing.
All the accused were convicted on five counts of attempted murder and spying with intent to sabotage.
The four were found to have planted a 150-kg (330-pound) Semtex bomb next to the dormitory block in Osnabrueck's Quebec Barracks. The soldiers escaped before the bombs wrecked the building.
The IRA is fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland.
